content.comment_body: I have a total of 6 [product_name] modules in my network, and 2 of them are inaccessible via [product_name] software, even though they are in RUN mode and show active LAN connectivity. These [product_name] modules don't have a display or buttons. My [product_name] operator panel has also lost access. Does anyone know how to resolve this?
Is your home network connected through a router, such as a Fritz!Box? If so, is DHCP enabled? Are the IP addresses of the [product_name] modules within the DHCP range?
Have you tried connecting the [product_name] module directly to your PC to see if that helps?

The modem includes a router that manages DHCP, and I haven't changed any settings. The IP addresses for the [product_name] modules are permanently set between x.x.x.60 and x.x.x.70. I've owned [product_name] modules with [article_no] since March 2020 and others with [article_no] since September 2022, always using fixed IPs. Until yesterday, everything worked smoothly. The only recent change was inserting a memory card into one module ([article_no]).

When DHCP is enabled, the router automatically assigns IP addresses, but it can't do this for the [product_name] modules, so they're not detected by the router. This could result in overlapping IPs with other devices like smartphones or laptops. I've assigned my [product_name] modules IPs outside the DHCP range. Why did you insert an SD card? Is the [product_name] program on the SD using a different IP address?

The SD card is new. Problem solved—the issue was a loose UTP connector leading to the other network switch in the experimental setup with the two [product_name] modules, the operator panel, and HMI. Reseating the connector restored access. Thanks for your help.
Problem resolved. Thank you for your assistance.

The SD card is new. Final update: the root cause was a loose UTP connector between switches on the experimental board with the two [product_name] modules, operator panel, and HMI. Fixing this restored connectivity. Thanks again for your support.

analysis.insight_summary: User faced loss of network connectivity for two [product_name] modules, even though they appeared to be running and had active network links. Access through both the configuration software and operator panels was disrupted. The issue was traced to a loose physical network connector, demonstrating how physical connection faults can suddenly interrupt device visibility in the system.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects stable and reliable access to all networked devices, straightforward troubleshooting steps, and clear diagnostics for hardware and operator panel connectivity issues.
